strategies.name: Monthly momentum
strategies.idea: Own the stocks that rose most over the past year, skipping the last month. Reshuffle once a month.

rule.measure: past-year return, skipping the last month
rule.check: on the last trading day of each month

strategies.name: Daily momentum
strategies.idea: Same idea as monthly momentum, but rechecked every day before the open.

rule.measure: past-year return, skipping the last month
rule.check: every trading day before the open

strategies.name: Profitability
strategies.idea: Own companies that turn the most gross profit per dollar of assets.

rule.measure: gross profit divided by total assets
rule.check: on the last trading day of each month

ideas.name: Monthly momentum
ideas.idea: Own the stocks that rose most over the past year, skipping the last month. Reshuffle monthly.

evidence.note: Strong in older studies; weaker after 2010 once costs are counted.

ideas.expected: About level with the S&P 500 after costs. Mainly a test that the machine works end to end.
ideas.stop_rule: Retire if it trails the S&P 500 by more than 1 point a year and the luck check is under 50%.

ideas.name: Daily momentum
ideas.idea: The same momentum idea, rechecked every day before the open.

evidence.note: Faster versions mostly lose their edge to trading costs.

ideas.expected: Below monthly after costs; worth seeing on paper because the backtest can't model daily fills well.
ideas.stop_rule: Stop if paper tracking drifts more than the agreed tolerance from its backtest.

ideas.name: Profitability
ideas.idea: Own companies that turn the most gross profit per dollar of assets. Reshuffle monthly.

evidence.note: Well supported, but in a narrow form; long-only results are weaker.

ideas.expected: A small edge over the S&P 500, smaller than published.
ideas.stop_rule: Retire if it trails the S&P 500 by more than 1 point a year in-sample.

exam.label: Final exam (2024 – Sep 2026)
exam.note: On hold until profitability has a finalist.

ideas.next: Paper book running; exam on hold.

ideas.name: Short-term momentum
ideas.idea: Last month's winners among the most-traded stocks. Reshuffle monthly.

evidence.note: One study says yes; two independent checks say it's about zero after costs.

ideas.expected: About zero to slightly negative after costs at 15 bp.
ideas.stop_rule: Retire both versions if neither beats the S&P 500 in-sample.

ideas.name: Earnings-reaction drift
ideas.idea: Buy stocks the market cheered most around their earnings release, hold for 20 days.

evidence.note: Mixed: the effect exists but much of it has faded since publication.

ideas.expected: About zero to negative after costs.
ideas.stop_rule: Written once its questions are answered.
ideas.next: Unblocks when the filing data lands.

ideas.name: Cash profitability
ideas.idea: Like profitability, but using operating cash flow instead of gross profit.

evidence.note: Supported as a stand-in; the exact measure isn't graded yet.

ideas.name: Filing changes → fundamentals
ideas.idea: When a company quietly rewrites its annual report, do its next results change?

evidence.note: Not enough evidence either way yet.

ideas.name: Insider buying
ideas.idea: Follow clusters of executives buying their own company's stock.

evidence.note: Routine insider buys don't predict much; clustered, opportunistic ones might.

ideas.name: Momentum + profitability
ideas.idea: Hold stocks that score well on both momentum and profitability.
ideas.parked: Waiting for a profitability finalist, so the combined test has something to stand on.

ideas.name: Trend filter
ideas.idea: Sit in cash when the market is below its 10-month average.
ideas.parked: Lowers risk but also return. Your goal is beating the S&P 500, so it's off the list.

families.name: Momentum
families.luck_bar_note: Each new try raises the bar the next result has to clear.

lessons.text: 12-1 momentum beat the market in long historical studies.
After 2010, net of costs, momentum's edge is weak and uneven.
Gross profitability predicts returns, in a narrow, long-short form.
Short-term earnings reactions mostly don't survive realistic costs.
